name: Brooding cinematic drone: three pulse-width-morph oscillators, opposed octave detune, single-osc vibrato, LFO PW breathing and split pitch-bend depths
goal: Build a massive, brooding cinematic drone in any capable synth: three pulse-width-morphing square oscillators (two an octave down, one wide 4-voice unison), the two low oscillators nudged slightly sharp and flat around the octave for clash, vibrato on only one oscillator, a slow LFO breathing one oscillator's pulse-width morph, a 12 dB low-pass on the mod wheel, reverb plus filtered delay, and different extra pitch-bend depths per oscillator so bends spread instead of moving in lockstep.

source.title: How to create Massive, Brooding, Cinematic Drones in any Synth

prerequisites: Synth with 3 oscillators offering pulse-width/shape morph, unison, per-osc vibrato routing, LFO, 12 dB low-pass, mod-wheel and pitch-wheel routing
Reverb and delay with high-/low-pass on repeats

steps.action: Use three oscillators, all set to a pulse-width-shifting square (a square whose pulse width can morph). Square/odd-harmonic content gives the hollow, brooding foundation.
Osc 1: move the shape slightly away from pure square for a biting edge, use 2 voices slightly detuned, add a slight vibrato, tune -12 semitones.
Osc 2: keep a square, tune -12 semitones, 4 unison voices detuned very wide.
Osc 3: leave at the higher (unshifted) pitch, give it a different pulse shape, 2 voices slightly detuned.
Amp envelope 'pad treatment': slow attack so the sound creeps in, long tapering release.

Add drama/clash: nudge the two octave-down oscillators by a small fraction in opposite directions (presenter's display: about -12.10 and -11.90) and offset Osc 3 slightly (~.5 in the synth's fine units).
steps.expect: Slow beating clash instead of a clinical tuning

steps.action: Restrict vibrato to one oscillator only; the others get none.
steps.expect: Movement without the whole stack wobbling

steps.action: Set pitch-bend range to +-1 so you can bend up and down by small amounts.
Assign a slow LFO to Osc 3's waveform/pulse-width morph for a little breathing.
Add a 12 dB low-pass (cascade-style) to tame harshness and map the mod wheel to cutoff; start notes with the mod wheel up and ride it.
Global FX: reverb with larger size and more wet so it holds on; then a delay (~140 in the presenter's units) with a little feedback and high-pass/low-pass on the repeats.
steps.expect: Large sustained space with filtered echoes

steps.action: Make bends spread: add a small extra pitch-wheel -> tune amount on Osc 1 (~20) and a larger one on Osc 3 (tried ~75, settled near 60 and then pulled slightly lower) so oscillators bend at slightly different rates.
steps.expect: Bends smear apart rather than moving in lockstep

verification: Held note fades in slowly and beats audibly from the opposed detune
Only one oscillator shows vibrato when soloed
Mod wheel down clearly darkens; up opens harshness
Pitch-wheel bend makes oscillators drift apart instead of moving in parallel
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there. Numbers quoted are the presenter's approximate values, in the source tool's own units.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only - map brand UI (Serum/Bitwig/Ableton/Logic/Cubase/Zebra/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for a Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid (Polyrhythm Studio); never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth/DAW vendors named in the source video.
Do not use the source synth's factory oscillator preset name; any pulse-width-morph square (or PWM via phase squeeze) is equivalent.

Distinct from cinematic-warm-analog-pad-drift-stereo and evolving-pad-unison-filter-swell-fifth: adds opposed octave detune, one-osc vibrato, PW-morph LFO and per-osc pitch-wheel depth spread for brooding drones.
